request: the owner, 2026-10-05: "The southern desert beach is the last empty stretch I can name. Build a wreck half-buried in the dunes -- something the water left behind, with an interior worth entering. Check it against Dustback in the south-east dunes first; if they are the same stretch, site them so they do not compete. Propose and build whatever else that ground supports. A desert meeting a sea should feel like neither."
name: the Brass Petrel
story: The Copperway (data/dune_ruin.json) brought its ore south across the dunes to this coast, and the company's barque, the Brass Petrel, carried it away. On her last call the Great Tide lifted her off the anchorage, carried her over the flats and drove her bow into the dune wall, where the sand closed over it to the rail. The ore is still in her hold; the master's log is still on the cabin wall; the sea never came back for her. In front of her the reef the tide threw up with her lies bleached and dead on the flats, and the things that live there now belong to neither the sea nor the sand: Galarian Corsola on the dead coral, Sandygast in the drift, and at the tide line a sandcastle that is not one.
ground_rule: Every Y is computed by tools/desert_wreck.py from tools/ground.py (the canonical heightmap, rounded). Nothing in this file is a Y except bounds, which the generator's own report prints and tests/test_desert_wreck.py holds equal to the plan. The deck D is max(ground under the transom row) + wreck.stern_show; the keel is D - wreck.depth. Every other piece stands on its own column's ground + 1.

site.dustback: NOT the same stretch. Dustback (data/resident_encounters.json) is anchored at (6244, 142, 6112), on the south-east dunes' plateau, about 700 blocks north-west of this site and 75 blocks higher; its 100-block migration scar ends at z6146. site.neighbours: the Copperway Khan (6744, 6224, data/dune_ruin.json) 600 blocks north-north-east, inland: the Petrel carried its ore, so the two tell one story from both ends without competing; the Glass Garden (5976, 6544, data/far_south.json) 560 west-north-west on the dune top; the Watcher's Ring (7056, 6200) 800 north-east; the beached wreck at (4070, 6584) (data/sea_life.json) 2400 west, a hull lying in the shallows on its side, where this one stands high and dry and swallowed; Pacifidlog's south jetty (5163, 63, 6658, data/ferries.json, planned) 1330 west along the same beach

wreck.why: a 40-block barque, beam 11, bow north into the dune wall, stern south on the flats. Level, not heeled: the dune climbed her, she did not climb it. The deck D is the sand at the transom + stern_show (4), so the stern stands 4 blocks of hull and a 4-block cabin over the flats, the sand rises along her side to 1-2 under the deck amidships, and at the bow the dune lies over the rail. The keel is D - depth (7), buried along her whole length. The hull narrows from the deck down (0 for 3 rows, 1 for 2, 2, then 3 at the keel). The hold is 5 rows of air on a floor 6 under the deck, beams across under the deck every 4 blocks; its bow end is choked with the sand that came through the stove-in bow (full to the deck to 6 from the bow, sloping to the floor at 10). A bulkhead at 29 closes the cargo hold from the crew's berth under the cabin; the stern's transom is stove in at the hold's level, the way in from the flats. The foremast stands out of the dune; the mainmast is broken over its yard and its top lies on the flats east of the hull.

spar.why: the mainmast's top, broken off and lying east of the hull across the flats: a stripped spruce log line (axis x) on each column's own ground + 1, from (wreck.x + 7, site z + 8), 11 long

anchor.why: the kedge she dropped too late: a chain lying on the sand from her starboard quarter south to the tide line, its anchor (a chipped anvil) at the end, half in the wash. Each link on its own ground + 1.

reef.why: the dead reef the tide threw up with her, bleached on the flats in front of the stern and running into the shallows: dead coral blocks, bone blocks and calcite where a value noise on a 5-block lattice (grid) is over threshold, 2 high over tall[0] and 3 over tall[1], thinning out over the last 6 blocks of its land edges; one block awash where the ground is one under the sea, nothing where it is deeper; a dead fan or a dead sprig on one dry head in three. All from a fixed hash, so a rebuild is byte-identical. A lane 5 wide (lane_half 2) runs from the water to the stove-in transom with nothing on it; the anchor chain's column and the resident's spot are kept clear. Dead coral is a spawn condition for Galarian Corsola and Cursola (data/spawn_blocks.json): here it is the point, and data/spawn_block_policy.json carries a whitelist entry scoped to this place.

flag.why: the castle's flag: a white banner on a spruce fence post two blocks east of the spot, so the place reads as a sandcastle before anything wakes

pool.band_why: tier 7 (data/encounter_design.json rules.tiers['7'], 38-48, cap 50), one under the dunes' tier 8 (south_east_dunes, 43-53). The beach is reached two ways: down the dune wall from the tier-8 sand sea, and along the strand from Pacifidlog's south jetty (data/ferries.json pacifidlog_south_jetty, 1330 blocks west on this beach), which data/towns.json sea_town calls 'an optional detour between badge 6 and badge 8'. A player off that ferry before gym 8 holds a cap of 50 at most, so the band's top (48) is under it and everything caught here is usable cold; the dunes above stay one tier harder, the way the strand is the easier edge of the sand. Sandygast's family matches east_coast_dunes' tier-7 Sandygast (38-46).

pool.entries_why: neither sea nor desert: sand ghosts (Sandygast), ghost coral (Galarian Corsola, Cursola), the barnacles on her hull (Binacle, the shore species data/sea_drift.json's isle uses), a sand snake (Silicobra), the berry-fermenting rock-dweller of shore caves (Shuckle), and, ultra-rare, the desert ruins' ghost slab (Galarian Yamask, whose own evolution needs sandy ground: Cobblemon 1.8.0 yamask.json). Every species verified in the Cobblemon 1.8.0 jar, with its evolution level read from it (2026-10-05). Weights are data/spawns.json rarity's family weights; an evolution above the band's floor is authored-only (weight 0), the habitat pools' rule (data/spawns.json driftmouth_isle_waters). Each spawnable position is tools/position_types.py choose() from the jar's own spawn files, written by records --write. Dhelmise, the wreck ghost, was considered and left out: every upstream spawn of it is submerged and it is 4.4 blocks tall, and the shelf in front is 1 block deep.
pool.blocks_why: two NATURAL ReplaceSpawns Habitat Blocks (the Route 1 mansion's ward's style, EXP-021): inside its range every ambient spawn is drawn from this pool instead of the pack's defaults. The strand's under the middle of the reef, one block under the sand; the hold's one block under the keel, 6 from the bow, under the sand-choked forepeak. They are 56 blocks apart, the sum of their ranges, so their spheres touch and do not overlap (an overlap spawns nothing, EXP-021). Between them a seam remains: cells of the aft berth more than 28 from both fall back to whatever the strip runs (docs/world-building/DESERT_WRECK.md). Neither is in a block the pack writes, so R9E can come before or after R9DW; R9DW is still put before R9E with the other block passes. A natural block placed by command is inert until its chunk reloads: restart after R9E (data/habitat_blocks.json's own procedure).

blocks.rule: vanilla 1.21.1 only. Lit only by lanterns (no light block, glowstone, sea lantern, shroomlight, torch or candle), no bubble-column block (soul sand, magma) and no water written. No chests (a chest is a Gimmighoul condition, tools/portals_audit.py) and no beds (a bed sets a respawn point, which the blackout's checkpoints own). The spawn conditions it does write are named in spawn_conditions and whitelisted in data/spawn_block_policy.json for this place.

blocks.palette_why: a tarred dark-oak bottom under spruce strakes, a birch deck the sun has bleached, stripped spruce for masts and beams: a ship of the sea. The reef is white and grey, dead coral, bone and calcite: the sea's colour gone out of it on the sand. Vanilla, as the Khan is, so the place adds no dependency.
